references.text: Hobab wishes to return to his land and his kindred, just as Abram was called to leave his land and his kindred to go to a new land.
Abraham sends his servant back to his land and his kindred to find a wife for Isaac, highlighting the importance of one's homeland and family.
Abraham speaks of his land and his kindred—the same words Hobab uses when expressing his desire to return home.
God commanded Jacob to return to his native land, illustrating the theme of returning to one's homeland.
Ruth refuses to leave Naomi and return to her people and her land, in contrast to Hobab's wish to do exactly that.
Hobab was a Midianite, and the book of Ruth mentions Jethro/Hobab's descendants through the Kenites who became part of Israel.
